posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
image959×161 17.4 KB

As you can see, /bin/ and /usr/bin/ are the same thing.
/bin/ is a symlink to /usr/bin/, hence both refer to the exact same binary.

The shebang (#! is called a shebang) simply tells the shell which binary to use to execute the script when run directly from the shell, here mentioning the bash binary using either path is equivalent.

EDIT: in your original post you have written /user/bin/bash instead of /usr/bin/bash that is totally wrong as /user does not exist.

Regards,
Sayan
